name: Hushim
overview: Hushim was a male descendant of the tribe of Dan, specifically identified as a son of Dan. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, highlighting his place within the early patriarchal narrative. The people associated with him are referred to as the Shuhamites, indicating a tribal or familial subgroup within Dan.
namesAndTitles: Hushim is the primary name given, with no specific meaning provided in the biblical record. He is also known as Shuham, another proper name without an indicated meaning. Both names appear in the Old Testament but do not carry explicit divine naming significance or etymological explanation in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hushim as a son of Dan, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text concerning Hushim.
scriptureSignificance: Hushim’s significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational Israelite family during the patriarchal period. The mention of the Shuhamites in the census of Israel’s descendants underscores his role in the genealogical and tribal structuring of Israel, particularly within the tribe of Dan. This connection situates Hushim within God’s providential plan for the nation of Israel.
